caption: Log: rings spaced by the logarithm of the distance - a zoom that never ends
why: Zooming into something means everything grows by the same proportion; rings spaced evenly in the logarithm of the distance look the same at every scale, so moving them looks like an endless zoom. Log - the natural logarithm - gives that spacing.
Its neighbours: Exp is the reverse; Divide gives one-over perspective; Log gives evenly spaced proportions.
steps: **Coords** `r`, the distance from the centre, is the **x** input.
Log of it is very negative near the middle and rises more and more slowly outward: rings by it are tight near the centre and wide at the edge, each the same ratio bigger than the last.
Times 1.5, minus a clock (**Time** times 0.3), into a **Wave**: the rings move outward and the pattern looks the same however far it goes - an endless zoom.
The wave is the **Palette**'s brightness; the same sum picks the colour.

try.label: Tighter
try.text: the Multiply at 3: twice the rings - a faster-looking zoom.

try.label: Zoom in
try.text: the clock's Multiply at -0.3: the rings move inward - zooming the other way.
